title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Competitive Methods - RFP
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: A public entity needs to procure a complex software system where experience, implementation methodology, and ongoing support are just as critical as the cost. Which sourcing method should be used?
options: Multi-step Invitation for Bids
Qualification-Based Selection
Request for Proposals (RFP)
Request for Quotations (RFQ)
questions.explain: An RFP is used when qualitative factors such as vendor experience and methodology must be evaluated alongside price to determine the best overall value for the agency.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following describes the key distinction between an IFB and an RFP?
options: An IFB is publicly advertised, whereas an RFP is only sent to prequalified vendors
An RFP permits the consideration of non-price factors to determine the best value, whereas an IFB is awarded solely on price and responsiveness
An IFB allows for negotiations after bid opening, while an RFP requires strict adherence to the submitted price
An RFP is used primarily for construction, while an IFB is used for consulting services
questions.explain: The fundamental difference is that IFBs are awarded based solely on the lowest price from a responsive/responsible bidder, whereas RFPs evaluate qualitative factors along with price to determine best overall value.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: During an RFP process, what mechanism ensures that qualitative factors are objectively and fairly reviewed?
options: Awarding strictly to the lowest price
Publicly revealing all technical proposals before scoring
Utilizing an evaluation committee and a structured, pre-established scoring matrix
Allowing the requesting department's director to pick their favorite proposal
questions.explain: RFPs use structured scoring matrices with predefined weights and a diverse evaluation committee to ensure that qualitative proposals are scored objectively.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: In a Request for Proposals (RFP), how is the 'Best Value' generally determined?
options: By dividing the lowest price by the number of pages in the proposal
By weighting technical merit, experience, and price according to the criteria stated in the solicitation
By holding a public auction until only one vendor remains
By excluding the highest and lowest prices and averaging the remainder
questions.explain: Best Value is determined by evaluating both cost and non-cost factors (such as technical approach and experience) based on the specific weights declared in the RFP.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following elements is critical to include in a formally advertised Request for Proposals (RFP), but is NOT required in an Invitation for Bids (IFB)?
options: A deadline for submission
Standard Terms and Conditions
The evaluation criteria and their relative importance/weights
The delivery address for the goods
questions.explain: An IFB does not need weighted evaluation criteria because price is the only factor. An RFP requires a clear statement of evaluation criteria and their relative importance so vendors know how they will be judged.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: In the RFP process, if a vendor submits a highly technical proposal that meets all operational needs but has a significantly higher price than competitors, the evaluation committee will:
options: Automatically reject it as non-responsive
Automatically award to it because technical quality overrules price
Score it based on the pre-established weighting of technical merit versus price
Convert the RFP to a Sole Source
questions.explain: In an RFP, price and technical merit are weighed against each other according to the published scoring rubric to determine the best overall value to the agency.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: An agency is evaluating RFP responses. Vendor A submitted the best technical proposal but the highest price. Vendor B submitted an acceptable technical proposal at a significantly lower price. Vendor C submitted a poor technical proposal at the lowest price. Who should win?
options: Vendor A automatically, because they are the most qualified
Vendor C automatically, because they have the lowest price
The vendor who yields the highest combined score based on the weighted criteria set forth in the RFP
The decision must be sent to a judge to determine fairness
questions.explain: In an RFP, award is made based on 'best value.' The scoring methodology established in the RFP mathematically determines which vendor represents the best balance of cost and qualitative factors.
